paper: Kandasamy et al. 2022, Int. J. Mol. Sci. 23, 14494 (DOI 10.3390/ijms232214494, PMID 36430971)
data: SRR14598288 (Illumina NovaSeq 6000, 14.8M PE); BioProject PRJNA731289; BioSample SAMN19277818
replication_verdict: PARTIAL (Coverage 8 / Agreement 8; 17 VERIFIED, 11 PARTIAL, 0 CONTRADICTED, 0 NOT_TESTED across 28 claims)

open_questions.q: Is the DJF10 bacteriocin arsenal a full two-cluster system as the paper reports (plantaricin J cluster + a sactipeptide cluster), or is the sactipeptide call a false positive of BAGEL4 on this draft assembly? The plantaricin cluster reproduced at 100% identity for four core peptides (plnF/J/N + 85% plnA) plus the plnG ABC transporter in a 7 kb window on NODE_10, but the sactipeptide cluster (paper AOI 1) was not detected by our Radical_SAM PF04055 + neighborhood surrogate. Three PF04055 hits exist genome-wide, all in metabolic (PFL activase, GTP 3',8-cyclase) context, not paired with a leader peptide and dedicated ABC transporter.
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md section 2.6 and claim 28 (PARTIAL+): plantaricin fully verified; sactipeptide surrogate came up empty and BAGEL4's RiPP HMM library is proprietary/web-only. Honest blocker explicitly named in Section 4.
next_steps: Rerun the assembly through BAGEL4's web service or a licensed RiPP-aware HMM pipeline (e.g., antiSMASH RiPP module, DeepRiPP, RRE-Finder) to test the sactipeptide call directly.
If a RiPP-aware scan still returns nothing, ask whether the paper's sactipeptide call was a BAGEL4-specific artefact and revise the claim to a single cluster.
Order or synthesize the predicted mature plantaricin peptides and test in-vitro antimicrobial activity vs a Gram-positive indicator panel to close the sequence-to-function gap.

open_questions.q: How does DJF10's probiotic-trait gene inventory (bile-salt hydrolase cbh at 99.7% identity, 10 Na+/H+ antiporters, 5 cold-shock cspA, full stress-response chaperone set groES/EL + clpB/C/E/L/P + hslO/V + dnaK/J, sortase A, hemolysin tlyA at 41.8% identity) compare quantitatively to well-characterized reference L. plantarum probiotic strains (WCFS1, 299v, ATCC 14917, Lp90, ST-III)? The paper asserts DJF10 is a probiotic candidate; our replication confirmed the individual gene presences but did not benchmark them comparatively.
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md claims 13-18 (all VERIFIED individually) but no cross-strain comparison performed. The paper's probiotic-candidate framing hinges on comparative rather than absolute inventory.
next_steps: Assemble a reference panel of 10-20 published L. plantarum probiotic and non-probiotic genomes, run identical Prokka + KEGG + CAZyme pipelines, and produce a presence/absence + %-identity matrix for the paper's asserted probiotic-marker gene set.
Compute pangenome roary/panaroo differentials between DJF10 and the reference panel to flag any DJF10-specific or DJF10-missing probiotic-associated loci.
Report whether the DJF10 inventory sits inside, on the edge of, or outside the reference-probiotic distribution for each marker.

open_questions.q: The paper reports no plasmids and our short-read assembly confirms zero replicons across three tools --- but plasmids can be lost during subculture and short-read assemblies systematically underdetect small circular replicons. Given DJF10 carries 14 IS elements (10 high-confidence) and 10-18 genomic islands, what is the actual horizontal-gene-transfer (HGT) risk profile for this strain in a probiotic delivery setting, and are any of the detected islands or IS-elements adjacent to loci of regulatory concern?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md claim 10 (no plasmids, VERIFIED), claim 21 (14 IS-family calls, VERIFIED), claim 27 (10-18 genomic islands, PARTIAL). Absence-of-plasmid claim is inspection-limited by short-read technology; HGT risk assessment for probiotic safety was not performed.
next_steps: Perform long-read (Nanopore or PacBio HiFi) resequencing of the DJF10 stock to definitively confirm zero-plasmid status and close any circular replicons the short-read assembly missed.
Reannotate each of the 10-18 candidate genomic islands and 14 IS elements for cargo genes, particularly any silent or truncated AMR / virulence / metabolic-shift genes.
Score the strain against the EFSA QPS and FDA GRAS transferable-resistance-gene criteria to produce a documentable HGT-risk profile.

open_questions.q: The paper reports 3 CRISPR arrays; our pipeline reported 1 high-confidence array (PARTIAL). Beyond count, is DJF10's CRISPR-Cas system complete (i.e., cas genes present, spacer repertoire mappable to known phage/plasmid sources), what subtype is it (Type I-E, II-A, III-A, etc.), and does the spacer content match the paper's asserted 3-array configuration?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md claim 20 (3 arrays paper, 1 detected, PARTIAL) --- our direct-repeat heuristic likely missed 2 arrays below threshold; cas-gene typing and spacer-target analysis were not performed at all.
next_steps: Re-run with CRISPRCasFinder and CRISPRDetect at multiple sensitivity settings to determine whether the missing arrays are simply below our threshold or genuinely absent.
Extract and blastn the spacer repertoire against phage and plasmid databases (phageDB, IMG/VR, PLSDB) to identify past HGT-defence encounters.
Type the cas-gene cassette (Cas1, Cas2, Cas3/Cas9/Cas10 signature) to place DJF10's system in the correct subtype and compare against the paper's implicit or explicit typing.

open_questions.q: The paper claims DJF10 is a probiotic candidate on the basis of in-silico evidence (safety-database screens, bile-salt-hydrolase presence, bacteriocin cluster presence). Our replication confirmed the genomic evidence but performed zero wetlab work. What is the actual in-vitro adhesion phenotype (Caco-2 or HT-29 binding), antimicrobial spectrum (against a standard Gram-positive and Gram-negative indicator panel), acid/bile survival curve, and cytotoxicity profile of DJF10 --- and do these phenotypes track the in-silico predictions?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md Section 5 (final verdict, explicit acknowledgment that probiotic-function claims are wetlab endpoints not addressable by in-silico replication) and the GENUINE CRITIQUE section 'What the report cannot yet claim'. The paper's central biological claim (probiotic candidate) is neither confirmed nor challenged by our work.
next_steps: Culture DJF10 from the deposited stock and run a standard probiotic-characterization panel: MRS growth curve, pH 2.5-3.0 survival for 3h, 0.3% oxgall bile survival for 4h, Caco-2 adhesion assay, agar-well antimicrobial screen vs Listeria/Salmonella/E. coli/S. aureus indicators, hemolysis assay on blood agar (predicted tlyA is low-identity so should be non-hemolytic).
Purify the predicted plantaricin peptides (from OQ1) and independently measure their MIC vs the indicator panel.
If in-vitro phenotypes match predictions, advance to a rodent tolerability + colonization study before making any probiotic-product claim.
